name: Southern Ocean Surf Reef ("Midds Reef")
coords: metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (Middleton Beach, near the 'Surfer's Beach' car park); x = alongshore (positive toward north — assumed from the apparent north-up orientation of the Bluecoast/ASR design figure [R3], which shows dunes/land to the west and open water to the east, consistent with Middleton Beach's real north-south shoreline trend; no explicit north arrow is printed on the figure, so this is an inference, see open_issues); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0

crest_depth_m.datum: below AHD (Australian Height Datum, ≈ mean sea level); ≈0.74 m below mean low water, ≈1.34 m below mean high water

distance_offshore_m.measured_from: shoreline / landward toe of the reef, per the Bluecoast/ASR concept-design table ('Cross-shore position: 140m from landward toe') reproduced on the City of Albany project page; our polygon's near (shoreward) tips sit at y=140-145 and its centroid sits at y≈189

orientation_notes: The Bluecoast/ASR 'Final Reef Design' table (reproduced as a figure on R3, filename design.jpg) specifies 'Crest orientation: Curved, 270°N-305°N... Maximises breaking and creates waves that peel evenly along the reef.' This is the bearing of the reef's own curved crest/wave-break line (a ~35 degree arc), not a stated swell-approach azimuth — no source we found gives a numeric swell-approach bearing (contrary to Gemini's invented '160-190 deg SSE-S', see gemini_comparison). The design table also specifies 'Surfing direction: Left-hander' and a 'Take-off area' at the more offshore, wider end of the reef (per the same figure), with the wave peeling toward the narrower, more shoreward end, matching R3's text 'the design provides surfing rides of up to 100m'. Our polygon therefore tapers to a point at its shoreward/updrift-adjacent end and bulges to its maximum ~110 m cross-shore width at the offshore 'take-off' end, per this figure — but the figure's own two dimension-arrow annotations (110 m and 140 m) do not share a consistent pixel scale (see derivation row 8), so this reading is topological/qualitative only, not a scaled tracing.
materials: Submerged rock-berm surf reef; ~62,800 t of layered granite in three graded layers — belly (D50 0.16 m, 12,400 t, 18%), core (D50 0.49 m, 23,600 t, 36%), Class 1 armour (D50 0.94 m, 26,800 t, 46%); no geotextile [R3]

derivation.quote_or_figure: design.jpg plan sketch shows a curved, elongated rock mound with a curved fan of wave-peel lines emanating from a corner near the shoreward tip and sweeping across a 'Surfing area' / 'Take-off area' overlay; RaisedWaterResearch's May-2025 construction-overview aerial (R10) shows a dark, elongated, diagonally-oriented submerged rock shadow tapering toward its shoreward end, with a barge working the wider, offshore end; ABC's aerial dredge photo (R2) shows a similar dark elongated patch beneath vessels
derivation.uncertainty: High. The design.jpg figure mixes the physical reef outline with an unrelated wave-refraction/peel-line fan (curved lines radiating from the take-off point across the surf/take-off zone overlays) — these curved lines are NOT the rock structure's edge and were excluded once recognised. The aerial construction photos are dated May 2025, mid-construction (per their own captions), so may show a partially-built extent rather than the final footprint. No true as-built survey or CAD outline was found.

derivation.quote_or_figure: "Reef volume: 34,000m3 (based on 2017 bathymetry) — Development costs approx. $11m, maximising the project budget" (Bluecoast/ASR design table, design.jpg)
derivation.uncertainty: This is an earlier, 2017-bathymetry-based concept-design estimate (matches the $11m/$11.75m committed-funds figure already in the card), not necessarily the final as-built volume. It is broadly consistent with the final 62,800 t tonnage at a plausible placed-rock bulk density (~1.6-1.9 t/m3 including voids, vs ~2.6-2.7 t/m3 for solid granite), which would imply ~33,000-39,000 m3 — no contradiction, but not independently confirmed.

derivation.quantity: figure internal scale consistency (methodology note, not a reef dimension)

derivation.method: Re-measured 2026-09-25 by pixel-tracing both dimension-arrow endpoints on design.jpg at 8-20x zoom with a labelled pixel grid, then cross-validated against the figure's own printed scale bar (0 to 0.1 km), which was independently measured twice (0-0.05 km and 0.05-0.1 km) and found self-consistent at 0.815 px/m.
derivation.quote_or_figure: Scale bar: 0.815 px/m (self-consistent). '140m' dimension arrow: endpoints at pixel (660,127)-(753,172) in the original 1026x521 design.jpg, length ≈103.3 px = 0.738 px/m. '110m' dimension arrow: endpoints at pixel (793,125)-(863,163), length ≈79.6 px = 0.724 px/m.
derivation.uncertainty: CORRECTED FINDING (2026-09-25 verification pass): the two dimension arrows are mutually consistent with each other (0.738 vs 0.724 px/m, only ~2% apart) — NOT a ~37% mismatch as an earlier draft of this file claimed (that figure, '2.73 px/m vs 1.99 px/m', could not be reproduced on careful re-measurement and appears to have been a pixel-identification error in the original pass). Both arrows do read a consistent ~10-12% shorter than the figure's own printed scale bar would predict for their labelled distances, which is more consistent with hand-placed/eyeballed dimension-line graphics than with a genuine internal scale contradiction. The figure is still not used for precise scaled-vertex tracing (out of caution, given this residual ~10% offset and the schematic nature of the annotations), but the polygon's 165x110 m envelope comes directly from the sourced text quotes, not from pixel tracing, so this correction does not change any reported dimension — only the methodology note.

open_issues: No true as-built plan-view CAD drawing or bathymetric survey was found publicly. The only plan-view figure available (design.jpg, legend 'ASR Design') is a pre-final concept sketch whose own two printed dimension arrows (110 m and 140 m) scale inconsistently by ~37% when pixel-measured — it was therefore used only for qualitative shape/taper topology, never for scaled vertex coordinates.

The design.jpg figure combines the physical reef outline with a separate wave-refraction/peel-line fan; distinguishing the two required close visual inspection and there remains some residual uncertainty about exactly where the rock structure's own edge lies versus the illustrative wave lines.

The two real aerial construction photos (R10, R2) are both dated/captioned May 2025, i.e. mid-construction — they may show a partially-built extent rather than the completed footprint, so were used only to corroborate general taper direction, not final size.

Exact polygon vertices are a low-confidence synthetic estimate, constrained only by the sourced 165 m x 110 m bounding envelope and the qualitative crescent curvature described in the design table; treat the polygon as illustrative of shape family, not a precise outline.
area_m2 (9,720) is not a published figure — it is a geometric consequence of our assumed polygon and should be treated as low-confidence, same caveat as Gemini's own area figures.

The x-axis 'positive = north' convention is inferred from the apparent north-up orientation of the design figure (land west, water east, coast trending N-S) rather than from an explicit stated bearing or printed north arrow — flagged as an assumption.

Distance offshore has a documented range across sources (120 m per Wikipedia/R4, 140 m per the current R3 page, ~145 m per a 2023 FAQ/R15) reflecting design evolution over time; we used the current page's 140 m figure as primary, consistent with the card.

Reef volume (34,000 m3) comes from an earlier 2017-bathymetry concept-stage table on the same figure as the shape sketch and may not equal the final as-built volume; only the final tonnage (62,800 t) is well corroborated across sources.

R15 (City of Albany, May 2023 FAQ PDF), read in full during the 2026-09-25 verification pass, gives an earlier interim design of 'up to 100 metres in width' (vs the final 110 m) and an interim footprint of 'approximately 16,000m2' (vs our ~9,720 m2 estimate and Gemini's unsourced 13,500/12,363 m2) — consistent with the card's existing 'design evolution over time' framing for the offshore-distance figure, now shown to also apply to width and area. The current R3 page's 165/110/140 figures were kept as primary, per existing methodology (prefer the final/current page over superseded interim estimates).

No individual designer name could be independently confirmed for this project as of the 2026-09-25 verification pass (see gemini_comparison.disagree, 'designer names'). Only the firm, Bluecoast Consulting Engineers, is confirmed (R3, R15's consultant-team list); a prior draft's attribution of 'Evan Watterson' to this specific project did not hold up against its own cited sources and was withdrawn.
